_README: One source of truth for the facts that appear on more than one page. This project is static hand-edited HTML with no build step, so this file cannot inject values — instead `npm run lint` reads it and FAILS when a page contradicts it (see 'canonical facts' in tools/lint.mjs). Change a shared fact here first, then fix the pages lint names. Provenance for each fact lives in data/parish-facts.json; this file is about keeping the pages consistent with it.

serviceTimes.note: Two distinct services. A single 9:00 start against both is the error the live parish site makes; never reproduce it. Feast-day Liturgy times are NOT covered by this confirmation and stay tagged TODO: verify.

contact.priestRoute: Contact the parish office to arrange a conversation with Fr. John.
contact.note: The parish office is the ONLY published route to Fr. John. Do not promise he is available immediately after Liturgy, and never publish his personal mobile.

terminology.fellowshipMealNote: The parish calls the post-Liturgy fellowship 'coffee hour'. It may be described as an agape/shared meal in passing, but 'the Agape Meal' must not be the primary label.
terminology.liturgyBookNote: Available from a greeter or in the pew. NOT a gift and not taken home — never call it complimentary, free or a take-home prayer book.
terminology.hallNote: Every page says 'the parish hall', and hall.html is titled that way. 'Community Hall' arrived with the Fellowship & Care brief on 2026-08-10 and was not used, because one building with two names across eighteen pages is how a site starts contradicting itself. NOT confirmed with the parish: if they call it the Community Hall, change this line and the forbidden pattern below FIRST, then fix the pages lint names.

worship.languagesNote: Confirmed by the parish. Congregational portions — the Creed, the Lord's Prayer — are offered in more than one language. Earlier drafts said 'mostly in English'; that is wrong.
worship.communion: Holy Communion is received by Orthodox Christians who are properly prepared to receive the Eucharist.
worship.antidoron: Antidoron is blessed bread that anyone may receive, including visitors who are not Orthodox. It is normally given by the priest after Divine Liturgy concludes, as people leave for the social hall. It is not Holy Communion.
worship.dress: Dress like you are meeting someone important. — Fr. John

parking.note: No visitor-specific parking and no overflow arrangement. Do not describe either.

bookstore.hours: Open every Sunday after Divine Liturgy
bookstore.stock: Orthodox books, pamphlets, prayer books, icons, prayer ropes, incense, crosses, candles and other devotional items

_ministriesNote: The list is settled for this presentation. Descriptions stay general: meeting frequencies, age and grade ranges, sports, retreats, camps and named charitable programmes are all unsourced and must not be restored. 'Choir & Chanters' has no ministry page on the live site and stays tagged TODO: verify.

links._fellowshipNote: The four destinations Fellowship & Care is built around. The parish plans to use SignUpGenius for coffee-hour hosting and potluck sign-ups, and Meal Train for meals to an individual household; mealSupportRequest is the PRIVATE route by which someone asks for help, and it must never be a public Meal Train page. None of the four exists yet, so all four are null and the page renders labelled inert buttons — each one marked with a TODO comment naming the key to fill in here. The button wording stays parish-facing ('Host a coffee hour'), not service-facing ('Go to SignUpGenius'): which tool handles the sign-up is our business, not the parishioner's.
links._nullNote: null means the destination does not exist yet. Render it as a clearly-labelled proposed placeholder — never invent a URL, and never leave a bare href="#" that looks live.

proposed._note: Presented in the demo as proposals for Fr. John's review. None of these exists today. Every one of them must carry the visible 'Proposed' label so the Parish Council can tell the difference.
items: The visitor welcome page behind a QR code (welcome.html)
A visitor experience survey, and someone to read it
Self-serve sign-up for the parish email list
Faces You Might See (names and photographs)
Meal trains for a parish household
A private request for meal support, and a coordinator to read it
Setup & cleanup, Children's corner and Missions as named ministries

canonical._note: Enforced by `npm run lint`. Each pattern is something a page must NOT say, because it contradicts a fact above. Adding an entry here is how a correction is made permanent instead of being quietly undone by the next edit.

forbidden.why: The parish calls it coffee hour. Use that as the primary label. Lower-case 'an agape meal', explaining the term in passing, is fine.
The Divine Liturgy book is not a gift and may not be taken home.
The Divine Liturgy book stays in the church.

The building is called the parish hall on every page and in hall.html's own heading. Pick one name. See terminology.hall — if the parish confirms 'Community Hall', change it there and here before changing any page.
There is no overflow parking arrangement.
No accessibility feature is confirmed. Do not claim one until the parish does.
Services are approximately 50% Greek and 50% English.
Sunday Divine Liturgy begins at 10:00 a.m.; Orthros begins at 9:00 a.m.
